instructions.8: Add the bouillon cube (if using) and stir well, then add the butter or oil and stir again.
instructions.9: Peel the potatoes, cut them into small cubes, and parboil in boiling water for 4 minutes.
instructions.10: Drain the potatoes and drop them into hot oil until crispy.

fah-124.title: Melt-in-Your-Mouth Brisket with Spiced Yellow Rice & Toasted Nuts
fah-124.chapter: Chapter 10: Fatma Abu Haty Channel Recipes
fah-124.culturalNotes: You can add nuts and coriander or parsley for garnish when serving. You can also drizzle white honey over the meat when serving for a slightly sweet taste.

instructions.1: Dry the brisket well.
instructions.2: Spread two tablespoons of mustard over the meat and massage it in.
instructions.3: Mix the paprika, salt, onion powder, and garlic powder and rub them over the meat.
instructions.4: Add two tablespoons of honey over the meat.
instructions.5: Heat a tray and add two tablespoons of oil.
instructions.6: Brown the brisket on all sides.
instructions.7: Spread the onion in the baking tray and moisten it with the salt, pepper, and two garlic cloves.
instructions.8: Place the browned brisket over the onion.
instructions.9: Add a quarter cup of BBQ sauce and a cup of boiling water.
instructions.10: Cover the tray with parchment paper and aluminum foil and place it in the oven on the lowest rack on high heat for half an hour.
instructions.11: Lower the temperature and leave the meat in the oven for 4 hours.
instructions.12: Slice the red onion and add the lemon juice and salt, mixing well.
instructions.13: Make the pickling mixture of sugar, salt, chili, vinegar, and mustard seeds and add it to the red onion.
instructions.14: Pulse the red pepper, lemon juice, parsley, tomatoes, and vinegar in the blender.
instructions.15: Add the salt and olive oil to the mixture and stir well.
instructions.16: Take the sauce from the meat and add it to the rice with the water and salt, stirring well.
instructions.17: Boil the rice and leave it on low heat until cooked.
instructions.18: Serve the meat with the rice, red onion, and sauce.

fah-125.title: Eid Meat with Onions & Tomatoes
fah-125.chapter: Chapter 10: Fatma Abu Haty Channel Recipes
fah-125.culturalNotes: Serve this dish with bread, rice, or pasta. You can also add some chopped parsley for garnish.

instructions.1: Cut the meat into small, evenly sized cubes.
instructions.2: Cut the onions into thin slices.
instructions.3: Cut the tomatoes into small cubes.
instructions.4: In a pot, place the mastic and ghee and let it melt and release its aroma.
instructions.5: Add the meat and brown it well until golden.
instructions.6: Add the bay leaf, black pepper, and spices and toss the meat until it takes a nice golden color.
instructions.7: Add the minced garlic and stir until fragrant.
instructions.8: Add the chopped onion and stir until wilted.
instructions.9: Add the sugar and stir well.
instructions.10: Cover the pot and leave on low heat until the meat starts releasing its steam.
instructions.11: Turn the meat from time to time and leave it on low heat until cooked.
instructions.12: Add the salt and tomato cubes and leave on low heat until fully done.
instructions.13: If the meat isn't cooked yet and the water runs out, add two tablespoons of hot water.
instructions.14: Serve hot with bread, rice, or pasta.

fah-126.title: Ossobuco with Carrots & Mushrooms
fah-126.chapter: Chapter 10: Fatma Abu Haty Channel Recipes
fah-126.culturalNotes: Serve the dish with white rice and sautéed vegetables. Instant bouillon is optional — good-quality meat doesn't need it.

instructions.1: Season the ossobuco pieces with the salt, pepper, and seven-spice on both sides.
instructions.2: Coat the pieces in the flour.
instructions.3: Heat a tablespoon of butter in a pan over the heat.
instructions.4: Brown the ossobuco pieces on both sides until nicely browned.
instructions.5: Remove the pieces from the pan and add the minced onion in their place.
instructions.6: Add the carrots and mushrooms and stir for a few minutes until the vegetables shrink.
instructions.7: Add the minced garlic and stir well.
instructions.8: Return the ossobuco pieces to the pan.
instructions.9: Add two cups of boiling water.
instructions.10: Add the packet of instant bouillon (optional).
instructions.11: Cover the pan and leave the meat over low heat for an hour to an hour and a half until cooked.
instructions.12: Serve the meat with white rice and sautéed vegetables.

fah-127.title: Cold-Cut Roast Beef (Trebeyanko)
fah-127.chapter: Chapter 10: Fatma Abu Haty Channel Recipes
fah-127.culturalNotes: Serve the cold meat with vermicelli rice or rice pilaf. The cooked meat keeps in the fridge for 2 days.

instructions.1: Take the trebeyanko roast and tie it with the kitchen twine.
instructions.2: Take a knife and make slits in the roast, then place the peppercorns, salt, whole pepper, and garlic in them.
instructions.3: Season the roast on the outside with the salt, whole peppercorns, ground cardamom, and thyme.
instructions.4: Leave the roast for half an hour to take on the seasoning.
instructions.5: Heat a little oil in a tray over the heat, then brown the roast on all sides until nicely colored.
instructions.6: Add the vegetables (onion, tomatoes, carrot, celery, bay leaf) to the tray.
instructions.7: Add two cups of boiling water, the sugar, and salt.
instructions.8: Cover the tray with aluminum foil, then a lid, and leave it over low heat for an hour.
instructions.9: After an hour, turn the roast and cover it again for another hour.
instructions.10: After two hours, let the roast cool, then refrigerate it overnight.
instructions.11: The next day, cut the roast into thin slices.
instructions.12: To make the vermicelli: dice the onion and bell peppers, then fry them in the oil and ghee until golden.
instructions.13: Add the vermicelli and stir until golden.
instructions.14: Add the remaining vegetables and toss them with the vermicelli.
instructions.15: Add the broth (boiling water) and let the vermicelli boil and absorb it.
instructions.16: Turn off the heat and let the vermicelli finish cooking in the residual heat.
instructions.17: Sauté the liver in oil with salt, pepper, and cinnamon (optional step).

fah-128.title: Smoked Meat
fah-128.chapter: Chapter 10: Fatma Abu Haty Channel Recipes
fah-128.culturalNotes: You can add fresh herbs like basil or coriander to the marinade for extra flavor. The smoked meat keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days.

instructions.1: Wash the meat well and cut it into medium-sized pieces.
instructions.2: Mix the salt, black pepper, cinnamon, cardamom, and turmeric in a bowl.
instructions.3: Place the meat in a deep bowl and add the mixed spices, crushed garlic, apple cider vinegar, and olive oil. Mix well until the meat is coated in the spices.
instructions.4: Cover the bowl and refrigerate the meat for at least two hours so it absorbs the spices.
instructions.5: After that, place the meat on a hot grill or in the oven at 180°C for an hour and a half until golden and smoky.
instructions.6: Serve hot with rice or bread.

fah-129.title: Slow-Cooked Clay-Pot Meat (Medamsa)
fah-129.chapter: Chapter 10: Fatma Abu Haty Channel Recipes
fah-129.culturalNotes: Serve the medamsa meat with white rice or rice ma'mar for a complete, tasty meal.

instructions.1: Prepare the marinade: in a large bowl, place the minced onion, salt, pepper, seven-spice, pinch of sugar, and bay leaves. Add a tablespoon of tomato paste and the 6 garlic cloves. Mix the ingredients well.
instructions.2: Add the diced tomatoes, whole small potatoes, and whole onion. Toss again to distribute the spices evenly.
instructions.3: Prepare the clay pot: place a layer of vegetables in the bottom of the pot, then a layer of meat, alternating until the pot is full.
instructions.4: Add 3 cups of boiling water over the mixture.
instructions.5: Seal the pot tightly with a dough made of flour and water.
instructions.6: Place the pot in the oven preheated to the highest temperature for 15 minutes, then lower the temperature to 150°C and leave for 3 hours.
instructions.7: When the time is up, open the pot carefully and enjoy the delicious slow-cooked meat.

fah-130.title: Orzo Pasta with Chicken
fah-130.chapter: Chapter 10: Fatma Abu Haty Channel Recipes
fah-130.culturalNotes: You can add more vegetables as you like, such as bell peppers and mushrooms. The dish keeps in the fridge for 2 days.

instructions.1: Heat the oil and ghee in a tray over the heat.
instructions.2: Add the chicken pieces and brown them on both sides until golden.
instructions.3: Add the curry, paprika, and salt and toss the chicken well.
instructions.4: Remove the chicken from the tray and set aside.
instructions.5: Add the onion and sauté until golden.
instructions.6: Add the orzo and toss it with the onion until toasted.
instructions.7: Add the carrots, bell peppers, and mushrooms (if you like) and toss the ingredients well.
instructions.8: Add the instant bouillon or boiling water with the salt and black pepper.
instructions.9: Add the chicken back and cover it with broth so it's submerged by about 2 cm.
instructions.10: Cover the tray and leave it over low heat for 3–4 minutes.
instructions.11: Stir the ingredients gently to distribute the broth evenly.
instructions.12: Cover the tray again and leave for 10 minutes until the orzo is cooked.
instructions.13: Add the fresh coriander and stir well.
instructions.14: Serve the dish hot.

fah-131.title: Mazaleeka (Mixed Liver & Offal)
fah-131.chapter: Chapter 10: Fatma Abu Haty Channel Recipes
fah-131.culturalNotes: You can serve mazaleeka with rice too. Make sure the heat is high so the liver comes out caramelized and tender.

instructions.1: Heat the oil in a pan over high heat.
instructions.2: Add the hearts, kidneys, and sweetbreads and sauté until their moisture dries up completely.
instructions.3: Add the cumin and black pepper while sautéing.
instructions.4: Add the garlic and stir until golden.
instructions.5: Add the liver slices and stir occasionally until cooked.
instructions.6: Add the salt and remaining black pepper and cumin.
instructions.7: Add the green pepper as you like.
instructions.8: Add the onion cut into wedges and stir for two to three minutes.
instructions.9: Add the grated tomatoes and leave for a minute or two.
instructions.10: Serve the mazaleeka hot with fino or baladi bread, tahini salad, and pickles.

fah-132.title: Pressed Lamb with Rice (Magh'loot)
fah-132.chapter: Chapter 10: Fatma Abu Haty Channel Recipes
fah-132.culturalNotes: You can use any kind of meat you like. You can also add vegetables like carrots and tomatoes for a richer dish.

instructions.1: Put oil in the pressure cooker and brown the meat pieces until golden.
instructions.2: Remove the meat pieces and set them on a side plate.
instructions.3: In the same pot, add the minced onion and sauté until it softens and turns golden.
instructions.4: Add the minced garlic and stir with the onion.
instructions.5: Add the spices (loomi, cinnamon, cloves, saffron, peppercorns, turmeric, coriander, ground cinnamon, ground black pepper, cumin, paprika, onion powder, garlic powder, meat spices, kabsa spices, curry) and toast them well.
instructions.6: Add the tomato paste and a pinch of sugar and toss the ingredients together.
instructions.7: Add the grated tomato and salt and toss the ingredients together.
instructions.8: Return the meat pieces to the pot and add boiling water to cover the meat.
instructions.9: Seal the pot and leave it over medium heat for 40 minutes.
instructions.10: After 40 minutes, open the pot and check the meat is cooked.
instructions.11: Add the rice and hot pepper and distribute evenly.
instructions.12: Seal the pot again and leave it over medium heat for 15 minutes.
instructions.13: After 15 minutes, open the pot and check the rice is cooked.
instructions.14: Garnish the dish with fresh coriander, nuts, and raisins.
instructions.15: Serve the dish hot.

fah-133.title: Hadhrami Mandi (Meat & Rice)
fah-133.chapter: Chapter 10: Fatma Abu Haty Channel Recipes
fah-133.culturalNotes: Make sure the oven is preheated for 30 minutes before adding the tray. You can extend the baking time depending on the type of meat. Serve the mandi hot garnished with nuts and fresh coriander.

instructions.1: Prepare the meat: mix the meat with the mandi spices, salt, and peppercorns. Rub the meat well so the fibers absorb the spices.
instructions.2: Prepare the sauce: in a pot over the heat, add the oil and butter. Add the minced onion and peppercorns and stir until fragrant. Add the grated carrots and raisins and stir well.
instructions.3: Prepare the broth: add the boiling water and bouillon cubes and stir until dissolved. Add the salt and let the sauce boil over the heat.
instructions.4: Prepare the rice: wash the rice well and place it in the baking tray. Strain the sauce over the rice and make sure the water covers the rice by about 2 cm.
instructions.5: Prepare the oven: place a rack over the tray or use perforated foil. Place the meat on the rack and cover it with parchment then foil. Seal the cover tightly.
instructions.6: Bake: place the tray in the oven preheated to 200°C for 15 minutes on the bottom rack, then move the tray to the middle rack and lower the temperature to 160°C. Bake for 3 hours and 15 minutes.
instructions.7: Serve: remove the tray from the oven and serve the mandi with the meat, nuts, and fresh coriander.

fah-134.title: Smoked Veal Shank
fah-134.chapter: Chapter 10: Fatma Abu Haty Channel Recipes
fah-134.culturalNotes: You can use lamb shank instead of veal shank. Seasoning the shank an hour before cooking gives a better taste. The cooked shank keeps in the fridge for 2 days.

instructions.1: Prepare the shank: season it with the salt, pepper, seven-spice, and cardamom.
instructions.2: Sear the shank: place the ghee in a pot over medium heat, then add the shank and brown it on all sides until golden.
instructions.3: Add the vegetables: add the onion, pepper, carrots, and herbs (rosemary, sage, thyme, bay leaves).
instructions.4: Add the water and broth:
instructions.5: Boil and cook: add the boiling water and the chicken bouillon cube, then cover the pot and leave the shank cooking over low heat until done.
instructions.6: Smoke: place the shank in a tray with a little charcoal and oil, then place it in the oven until it takes on a smoky aroma.
instructions.7: Serve: serve the shank with smoked rice and nuts.

fah-135.title: Chicken Nuggets
fah-135.chapter: Chapter 10: Fatma Abu Haty Channel Recipes
fah-135.culturalNotes: The nuggets keep in the freezer for up to a month. When frying, make sure the oil is hot enough so the nuggets don't stick.

instructions.1: Wash the chicken and cut it into small cubes.
instructions.2: Soak the chicken in water with lemon juice briefly, then rinse and dry it.
instructions.3: Place the chicken in the food processor with the spices, mustard, and starch and blend until you get a smooth mixture.
instructions.4: Mash the potatoes and fold them into the chicken mixture with the eggs.
instructions.5: Knead the mixture well until uniform.
instructions.6: Spread the mixture in an open freezer bag and sprinkle flour over it.
instructions.7: Cut the mixture into small squares.
instructions.8: Dip the nuggets in the flour, then the beaten egg, then the coarse breadcrumbs.
instructions.9: Arrange the nuggets on a plate separated by cling film if you're going to freeze them.
instructions.10: Fry the nuggets in hot oil over medium heat until golden.

fah-136.title: Chicken Parcel (Foil-Baked)
fah-136.chapter: Chapter 10: Fatma Abu Haty Channel Recipes
fah-136.culturalNotes: You can add any other vegetables you like. Serve the parcel with rice and salad for a complete meal.

instructions.1: Take a baking tray and line it with aluminum foil.
instructions.2: Add a sheet of parchment over the foil.
instructions.3: Place the chicken pieces in the tray.
instructions.4: Add the seasonings: salt, black pepper, paprika, onion powder, cardamom, seven-spice, tomato paste, and honey.
instructions.5: Toss the chicken well until coated in the seasonings.
instructions.6: Add the mixed vegetables (bell peppers, potatoes, carrots, celery, tomatoes, mushrooms, and beans) over the chicken.
instructions.7: Toss the mixture well until the vegetables are coated in the seasonings.
instructions.8: Cover the tray with parchment, then seal the foil tightly.
instructions.9: Place the tray in the oven preheated on high for 15 minutes, then lower the heat and leave for an hour.
instructions.10: After an hour, open the tray and check the chicken and vegetables are cooked.
instructions.11: Place the tray under the broiler for a few minutes until nicely golden.
instructions.12: Serve the parcel hot with rice and salad.

fah-137.title: Meat Parcel (Foil-Baked)
fah-137.chapter: Chapter 10: Fatma Abu Haty Channel Recipes
fah-137.culturalNotes: You can add two tablespoons of oil or ghee before sealing the parcel if you like. Serve with white rice, basmati rice, or rice with vermicelli.

instructions.1: Cut the meat into small cubes.
instructions.2: Cut the onions into wedges.
instructions.3: Place the onions in a bowl, add the salt, pepper, cumin, and seven-spice, and rub the onions well.
instructions.4: Add the minced garlic and toss.
instructions.5: Add the carrots, potatoes, celery, bay leaves, and hot or sweet peppers, and toss well.
instructions.6: Add the meat and toss until it absorbs the marinade.
instructions.7: Add the tomato sauce and the tomatoes cut into wedges, and toss well.
instructions.8: Wrap the parcel using aluminum foil and parchment paper.
instructions.9: Place the parcel in the baking tray.
instructions.10: Heat the oven to 220°C for 10 minutes.
instructions.11: Lower the temperature to 160°C and leave for two hours.
instructions.12: When the time is up, open the parcel carefully to avoid the steam.
instructions.13: Serve with rice, salads, and pickles.

w-ma-001.title: Lamb Börek

instructions.1: Heat the olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Add the onion and sauté for 5 minutes until soft.
instructions.2: Add the garlic and sauté for 1 minute. Add the ground lamb and cook for 5 minutes until browned.
instructions.3: Add the cumin, coriander, cinnamon, paprika, allspice, cayenne pepper, black pepper, salt, currants, and pine nuts. Stir well.
instructions.4: Add the tomato passata and water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes.
instructions.5: In a small bowl, whisk the egg with the yogurt. Add the egg mixture to the lamb and stir well.
instructions.6: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Place a sheet of phyllo pastry on a work surface and brush with melted butter. Repeat with 3 more sheets.
instructions.7: Add the lamb mixture to the top sheet and roll to form tubes. Place the tubes in a buttered baking dish.
instructions.8: Repeat the process until all the sheets and filling are used. Sprinkle with sesame seeds if desired.
instructions.9: Bake the börek for 25-30 minutes until golden and crispy.
instructions.10: To make the yogurt sauce, mix the yogurt, garlic, lemon juice, olive oil, and salt in a bowl. Serve with the börek.

w-ma-001.culturalNotes: Börek is a popular dish in Morocco, also known as lamb börek. It is often served on special occasions.

w-ma-002.title: Baba Ghanoush with Roasted Garlic

instructions.1: Preheat the oven to 475F.
instructions.2: Poke holes in the eggplant and rub it with olive oil. Place the eggplant and garlic head on a roasting pan wrapped in foil.
instructions.3: Roast the eggplant, turning occasionally until they collapse. Large eggplant will take 30-45 minutes.
instructions.4: Roast the foil-wrapped garlic for 20 minutes, then remove it from the oven and let it cool.
instructions.5: Toast the pine nuts in a dry skillet over medium heat until golden brown, stirring constantly.
instructions.6: Add half of the pine nuts to a food processor, reserving the other half for garnish. Pop the garlic cloves out of the skins and add them to the processor as well.
instructions.7: Scoop out four cups of eggplant flesh and add it to the processor with lemon juice, tahini, and parsley. Pulse, drizzling in olive oil as needed until the mixture reaches a hummus-like consistency.
instructions.8: Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.

w-ma-002.culturalNotes: Baba Ghanoush is a popular dish in Moroccan and Eastern cuisine, served as a dip with Arabic bread.

w-ma-003.title: Moroccan Semolina Pancakes - Beghrir

instructions.1: Combine all ingredients in a blender or food processor and blend on medium to high speed for one minute to achieve a smooth, creamy batter. If you notice anything sticking to the pitcher or bowl, stop to scrape down the sides.
instructions.2: Transfer the batter to a bowl and cover with plastic wrap. Let it rest for 10 to 15 minutes until the batter appears light and foamy with lots of tiny bubbles.
instructions.3: Heat a nonstick crepe pan over medium heat. When hot, stir the beghrir batter with a ladle, then slowly pour some batter into the center of the pan, allowing it to spread outward on its own.
instructions.4: Cook the pancake without turning until set with no wet spots, about one to two minutes. You can test the pancake by touching it lightly; it should feel spongy and no batter should stick to your finger.
instructions.5: Transfer the pancake to a clean towel to cool. Repeat with the remaining batter, adjusting the heat if necessary to prevent the bottoms of the pancakes from becoming overly brown.
instructions.6: Serve the beghrir dipped in syrup made from melted butter and honey, or with toppings and spreads on the side.

w-ma-003.culturalNotes: Beghrir is a traditional Moroccan breakfast dish, typically served with honey and melted butter.

w-ma-004.title: Bessara

instructions.1: Soak the dried split fava beans in water for at least 12 hours.
instructions.2: Drain and rinse the fava beans thoroughly.
instructions.3: Place the fava beans in a pot with water and bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for 30-40 minutes until tender.
instructions.4: Add the garlic, paprika, cumin, and salt, and stir well.
instructions.5: Use a hand blender or food processor to blend the fava beans until smooth.
instructions.6: Add lemon juice to taste.
instructions.7: Serve hot, garnished with ground cumin, ground cayenne, harissa, and extra virgin olive oil.

w-ma-004.culturalNotes: Bessara is a traditional Moroccan dish served as a soup or dip. It is typically served in a traditional earthenware bowl.

w-ma-005.title: Boulfaf

w-ma-005-i2.name: thin layer of sheep's caul fat

instructions.1: Wash the liver and cut it into small pieces.
instructions.2: Mix the liver with cumin, sweet paprika, cayenne pepper, salt, and ground coriander seeds.
instructions.3: Wash and dry the sheep's caul fat.
instructions.4: Wrap the liver pieces in the sheep's caul fat.
instructions.5: Grill the boulfaf until golden brown and well-cooked.

w-ma-005.culturalNotes: Boulfaf is a traditional Moroccan dish often served on special occasions.

w-ma-006.title: Almond Briouat

instructions.1: Blanch and peel the almonds by soaking them in water for 10 minutes, then rub to remove the skins.
instructions.2: Mix the peeled almonds with sugar, cinnamon, salt, mastic gum powder, and melted butter. Add orange flower water and knead the mixture well.
instructions.3: Cut the warqa into small squares. Place a small spoonful of the almond mixture in the center of each square and fold the edges to form triangles.
instructions.4: Heat the oil in a deep frying pan and fry the briouats until golden brown. Remove and drain on paper towels.
instructions.5: Heat the honey with a small spoonful of orange flower water. Dip the briouats in the warm honey and let them cool.
instructions.6: Serve the briouats cold, garnished with sesame seeds.

w-ma-006.culturalNotes: Briouat is a traditional Moroccan sweet served on special occasions and celebrations.

w-ma-007.title: Chebakia

w-ma-007-i9.name: mastic or gum arabic drops
w-ma-007-i9.standardAmount: 1/4 teaspoon, mixed with 1/4 teaspoon sugar and crushed to a powder

instructions.1: Clean and toast the unhulled sesame seeds in a dry pan until golden brown. Let them cool.
instructions.2: Mix the flour, baking powder, salt, anise, cinnamon, saffron, turmeric, and mastic in a large bowl.
instructions.3: Add the egg, melted butter, olive oil, vinegar, orange flower water, and dissolved yeast. Mix well until the dough is smooth and consistent.
instructions.4: Cover the dough and let it rest for two hours in a warm place.
instructions.5: Roll out the dough on a floured surface and cut it into small pieces. Shape each piece into a spiral or flower.
instructions.6: Fry the chebakia in hot vegetable oil until golden brown. Remove and drain on paper towels.
instructions.7: Mix the honey with orange flower water. Dip the chebakia in the warm honey mixture and let it cool.
instructions.8: Garnish the chebakia with toasted sesame seeds and serve.

w-ma-007.culturalNotes: Chebakia is a traditional Moroccan sweet typically served during Ramadan. It is known for its sweet and complex flavor and beautiful shape.

w-ma-008.title: Eggplant Chermoula Salad

w-ma-008-i5.name: white vinegar
w-ma-008-i5.standardAmount: 2 tbsp (or fresh lemon juice to taste)

instructions.1: Cut the eggplants into large cubes.
instructions.2: Soak the eggplants in salted water for 10 minutes, then drain.
instructions.3: Heat the olive oil in a pan over medium heat, add the eggplants and cook for 10 minutes until tender.
instructions.4: Add the chermoula paste, salt, and white vinegar (or fresh lemon juice), and continue to stir for 5 minutes.
instructions.5: Transfer the eggplants to a serving dish, and let it cool slightly before serving.

w-ma-008.culturalNotes: Chermoula is a traditional Moroccan marinade used in many dishes, known for its rich and spicy flavor.

w-ma-009.title: Sweet Couscous (Bil Zbib)

instructions.1: In a small pot, combine the raisins, dried apricots, and water. Bring to a boil.
instructions.2: Add the couscous, cover the pot, and turn off the heat. Let it sit for 5 minutes.
instructions.3: Add the butter, cinnamon, and sugar. Gently fluff the couscous, then pile it on a small shallow platter.
instructions.4: Dust with powdered sugar.
instructions.5: Serve warm or cool.

w-ma-009.culturalNotes: Sweet couscous is a traditional Moroccan dish served as a dessert or light meal.

w-ma-010.title: Ghoriba with Honey

instructions.1: In a large bowl, mix the eggs, egg white, sugar, vegetable oil or melted butter, vanilla, and warm honey.
instructions.2: Add the flour, baking powder, salt, and lemon zest, and mix well until the dough is smooth and consistent.
instructions.3: Cover the dough and let it rest for 15 minutes.
instructions.4: Shape the dough into small balls.
instructions.5: Place the dough balls on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, and brush them with the beaten egg yolk.
instructions.6: Bake the ghoriba in a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F) for 15 minutes or until golden brown.
instructions.7: Let the ghoriba cool before serving.

w-ma-010.culturalNotes: Ghoriba is a traditional Moroccan sweet typically served on special occasions and celebrations.

w-ma-011.title: Moroccan Semolina Cookies with Anise, Raisins and Sesame - Baked Harcha

instructions.1: Preheat the oven to 170°C (338°F). Line two baking sheets with parchment paper.
instructions.2: In a large bowl, mix the fine semolina, all-purpose flour, sugar, baking powder, salt, sesame seeds, anise seeds, and raisins.
instructions.3: Add the vanilla, eggs, melted butter, and milk. Mix well until the dough is smooth.
instructions.4: Shape the dough into small balls and place them on the baking sheets. Press each ball with a spoon to flatten it.
instructions.5: Sprinkle each ball with coarse or fine semolina and sugar.
instructions.6: Bake the cookies in the oven for 15 minutes or until golden brown.
instructions.7: Let the cookies cool on the baking sheets for 5 minutes, then transfer them to a wire rack to cool completely.

w-ma-011.culturalNotes: Moroccan harcha is a traditional type of cookie often served on special occasions and celebrations.

w-ma-012.title: Moroccan Harira Soup

w-ma-012-i17.name: tomato paste (combined with 1 or 2 cups water)

w-ma-012-i20.name: lemon wedges and cilantro (optional) for garnish

instructions.1: Soak the chickpeas and lentils in water for at least 8 hours or overnight.
instructions.2: In a large pot, heat the oil over medium heat. Add the meat and stir until golden brown.
instructions.3: Add the bones (if using), tomatoes, chickpeas, lentils, onion, celery, parsley, cilantro, smen (if using), salt, ginger, black pepper, cinnamon (if using), and turmeric. Mix the ingredients well.
instructions.4: Add enough water to cover the ingredients. Bring the soup to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for an hour and a half or until the chickpeas and lentils are tender.
instructions.5: Add the tomato paste mixed with water, rice or broken vermicelli, and flour mixed with water. Stir well and bring the soup to a boil again for 10 minutes.
instructions.6: Serve the harira hot, garnished with lemon wedges and cilantro if desired.

w-ma-012.culturalNotes: Harira is a traditional Moroccan soup often served during Ramadan. It is an ideal breakfast meal to start the day.

w-ma-013.title: Moroccan Khlea

instructions.1: Wash the gueddid thoroughly and cut it into small pieces.
instructions.2: Add the gueddid to a large pot with water and bring to a boil for 30 minutes.
instructions.3: Strain the gueddid and transfer it to another bowl with the chopped beef suet, salt, ground cumin seeds, crushed garlic, and ground coriander seeds.
instructions.4: Add the extra virgin olive oil and mix the ingredients well.
instructions.5: Return the gueddid to the pot and add enough water to cover it.
instructions.6: Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for 3-4 hours until it becomes tender.
instructions.7: Check the readiness of the khlea by trying a piece; it should be soft and easy to chew.
instructions.8: Once done, strain the khlea and transfer the fat to a separate bowl.
instructions.9: Return the khlea to the pot and add enough fat to cover it.
instructions.10: Let the khlea cool, then store it in an airtight container with the fat.
instructions.11: Store the khlea in the refrigerator for up to 6 months.

w-ma-013.culturalNotes: Khlea is a traditional Moroccan dish made from preserved meat in fat. It is used in many traditional Moroccan dishes.

w-ma-014.title: Méchoui (Leg of Lamb with Dried Fruit Stuffing)

instructions.1: Chop the onion and dried fruits, and add them to a skillet with rice, broth, salt, pepper, and ground coriander. Cover and simmer for about 10 minutes.
instructions.2: Prepare the lamb for stuffing and preheat the oven to 325F (165C).
instructions.3: If you choose to stuff the lamb, lay the slightly cooled rice and fruit mixture along the meat. Reserve extra stuffing in a casserole to bake.
instructions.4: Roll the leg of lamb back up and tie with butcher's twine.
instructions.5: Roast for 2.5 to 3 hours (or 25 minutes per pound of meat plus stuffing, plus an extra 25 minutes for medium). Add the small casserole of stuffing in the last 30-45 minutes of roasting, covering if it seems to be drying out.
instructions.6: Let the meat rest about ten minutes before slicing.
instructions.7: Serve with extra stuffing.

w-ma-014.culturalNotes: Méchoui is a traditional Moroccan dish served on special occasions. It is characterized by the rich flavors of lamb and dried fruits.

w-ma-015.title: Makroudh

instructions.1: In a food processor with the dough blade attached, mix the flour, salt, and olive oil together, scraping the sides once or twice.
instructions.2: Once all the grains are coated with oil, drizzle in the warm water until the mixture begins to pull together into a ball. Some of it will be moist, and a little bit will be dry.
instructions.3: Remove it all and knead together for a few minutes until a smooth ball forms. Cover and let rest for 10 minutes.
instructions.4: Cut pieces of the dough and roll them into snakes, then cut the snakes into 1.5-inch pieces. Press each piece with a fork to make little indentations.
instructions.5: Bring a pot of water to a boil and cook the makroudh for 10-15 minutes, depending on the thickness.
instructions.6: After cooking, drain the makroudh and coat it with a few spoonfuls of toum (lemon garlic sauce).

w-ma-015.culturalNotes: Makroudh is a traditional Moroccan dish often served on special occasions.

w-ma-016.title: M'rouzia

instructions.1: Mix the lamb with Ras-el-hanout and ground pepper. Let it marinate for 30 minutes.
instructions.2: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the lamb and brown on all sides.
instructions.3: Add the chopped onion, ginger, smen, salt, cinnamon stick, and saffron. Cook for 5 minutes until the onion is golden.
instructions.4: Add enough water to cover the lamb. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for an hour and a half until the lamb is tender.
instructions.5: Add the raisins, Ras el Hanout, cinnamon, and honey. Cook for 15 minutes until the raisins are soft.
instructions.6: In a separate pan, fry the almonds until golden. Set aside.
instructions.7: Serve the M'rouzia hot, garnished with the fried almonds.

w-ma-016.culturalNotes: M'rouzia is a traditional Moroccan dish served on special occasions and celebrations.

w-ma-017.title: Moroccan Msemen

w-ma-017-i8.name: fine semolina
w-ma-017-i8.standardAmount: 1/2 cup (can use coarser caliber if you like)

instructions.1: Mix the flour, semolina, sugar, salt, and yeast in a large bowl.
instructions.2: Gradually add the warm water and knead the ingredients until the dough becomes smooth and elastic.
instructions.3: Cover the dough and let it rest for 30 minutes.
instructions.4: Divide the dough into small balls.
instructions.5: Roll out each ball using a fork or your fingers until it is very thin.
instructions.6: Heat a skillet over medium heat and add a little oil.
instructions.7: Place the flattened dough in the skillet and fry it on both sides until golden brown.
instructions.8: Repeat the process with the remaining dough balls.
instructions.9: Serve the msemen hot with butter and fine semolina.

w-ma-017.culturalNotes: Msemen is a traditional Moroccan dish usually served with tea or as a breakfast meal.

w-ma-018.title: Moroccan Pastilla

w-ma-018-i17.name: salt and freshly ground black pepper

instructions.1: Heat the oil in a large frying pan.
instructions.2: Add the chicken and fry until golden brown.
instructions.3: Turn the thighs over and cook for a few more minutes, then remove them from the pan.
instructions.4: Add the butter to the pan and when it has melted, add the onions and fry over low heat until soft.
instructions.5: Add the garlic and spices and fry for a few more minutes.
instructions.6: Return the chicken to the pan and add the stock.
instructions.7: Season, then cover the pan and simmer for about half an hour or until the chicken is tender. Remove the chicken and set it aside.
instructions.8: When the chicken is cool enough to handle, finely chop the meat.
instructions.9: Return the liquid to the heat and reduce it by half.
instructions.10: Add the eggs to the liquid and continue to cook over low heat until you have a mixture that resembles loose scrambled eggs.
instructions.11: Add the ground almonds and stir, then add the dates, orange blossom water, zest, and finally, the chicken.
instructions.12: Remove the pan from the heat and allow to cool.
instructions.13: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees Fahrenheit.
instructions.14: To assemble the pastilla, use a 9-inch pie plate or tin.
instructions.15: Take a sheet of filo pastry and brush it with melted butter. Place it in the dish, gently pushing it into the edges without tearing.
instructions.16: Repeat with another sheet of filo, this time placing it at a right angle to the first.
instructions.17: Repeat with two more sheets of filo, this time placing them on the diagonal.
instructions.18: Spread the filling over the pastry. Fold over the overhanging pieces of filo in reverse order – they should just about cover the filling.
instructions.19: Take the remaining two pieces of filo and cut them to fit the dish.
instructions.20: Brush them with butter, then cover the pastilla, tucking under any edges.
instructions.21: Bake in the oven for about 30 minutes until the pastry is a crisp, golden brown.
instructions.22: Remove from the oven and allow to cool a little before dusting it with powdered sugar and cinnamon.

w-ma-018.culturalNotes: Pastilla is a traditional Moroccan dish that combines sweet and savory flavors, often served on special occasions.

w-ma-019.title: Moroccan Chicken with Preserved Lemon and Olives

instructions.1: Wash the chicken and cut it into pieces. Place it in a bowl and sprinkle with salt, saffron, ginger, turmeric, black pepper, smen, chopped coriander, and parsley. Mix well and let it marinate for 30 minutes.
instructions.2: In a large pot, heat the oil and sauté the onions until golden brown. Add the garlic, turmeric, and salt, and stir for a minute.
instructions.3: Add the chicken pieces to the pot and stir until they turn golden. Add water to cover the chicken and bring to a boil. Then reduce the heat and let it simmer for 30 minutes.
instructions.4: Add the chicken livers (if using), preserved lemon, and olives. Mix well and let it cook for an additional 10 minutes.
instructions.5: Serve the chicken hot with rice or Moroccan bread.

w-ma-019.culturalNotes: Moroccan Chicken with Preserved Lemon and Olives is a traditional dish in Moroccan cuisine, often served on special occasions and family gatherings.

w-ma-020.title: Meknes Style Rfissa

instructions.1: Wash the chicken and cut it into small pieces.
instructions.2: In a large pot, heat the olive oil and sauté the onions until golden brown.
instructions.3: Add the spices (ras el hanout, black pepper, ginger, turmeric, salt, cayenne pepper, saffron) and stir for a minute.
instructions.4: Add the chicken and stir until it is coated with the spices.
instructions.5: Add the tomatoes, garlic, parsley, cilantro, za'atar, fliou, merseta, fenugreek seeds, lentils (if using), and smen (if available).
instructions.6: Add water to cover the ingredients and bring to a boil.
instructions.7: Reduce the heat and simmer for an hour and a half until the chicken is cooked.
instructions.8: Add the shredded msemen and simmer for another 15 minutes.
instructions.9: Serve the rfissa hot, garnished with ground fried almonds, dates, and hard-boiled eggs.

w-ma-020.culturalNotes: Rfissa is a traditional Moroccan dish served on special occasions, such as holidays and family gatherings.

w-ma-021.title: Seffa Medfouna

instructions.1: Wash the broken vermicelli and drain it. Place it in a large bowl and add 3 tablespoons of oil and 2 teaspoons of salt. Mix well.
instructions.2: Place the broken vermicelli in a colander and drain it well. Place it in a steamer and steam for 30 minutes.
instructions.3: While steaming, soak the raisins in water for 20 minutes.
instructions.4: In another bowl, mix 4 tablespoons of unsalted butter with 1/2 cup of powdered sugar. Mix well and set aside.
instructions.5: In a large pot, melt 4 tablespoons of unsalted butter and 1/4 cup of olive oil. Add the chopped onions and sauté until golden brown.
instructions.6: Add the chicken pieces and spices (ginger, salt, white pepper, black pepper, cinnamon sticks, saffron, turmeric). Cook for 10 minutes.
instructions.7: Add 2 cups of water and simmer the chicken on low heat for 45 minutes until cooked.
instructions.8: In a small bowl, mix 1 cup of powdered sugar with 2 tablespoons of ground cinnamon.
instructions.9: After steaming, place the broken vermicelli in a large bowl and add the butter and sugar mixture. Mix well.
instructions.10: Place the broken vermicelli in a serving dish and add the chicken and sweet mixture. Garnish with fried and ground almonds, chopped cilantro, and caramelized raisins (if desired).

w-ma-021.culturalNotes: Seffa Medfouna is a traditional Moroccan dish served on special occasions. It is characterized by its rich spice blend and toasted almonds.

w-ma-022.title: Moroccan Sellou

w-ma-022-i8.name: mastic gum
w-ma-022-i8.standardAmount: several drops, ground to a powder (optional)

instructions.1: Fry the almonds in vegetable oil until golden brown, then let them cool.
instructions.2: Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan until golden brown, then let them cool.
instructions.3: In a large bowl, mix the flour, powdered sugar, cinnamon, anise, salt, and mastic gum (if available).
instructions.4: Add the toasted almonds and sesame seeds to the flour mixture and mix well.
instructions.5: Melt the butter in a pan over low heat, then add it to the mixture and mix well until you get a cohesive dough.
instructions.6: Shape the dough into small balls and place them on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
instructions.7: Bake the balls in a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F) for 15-20 minutes until golden brown.
instructions.8: Let the balls cool completely before serving.

w-ma-022.culturalNotes: Sellou is a traditional Moroccan sweet served on special occasions such as holidays and weddings.

w-ma-023.title: Shakshouka

instructions.1: Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the red bell peppers, Anaheim peppers, onion, and garlic. Brown the vegetables for 15-30 minutes until they are soft and browned.
instructions.2: Add the tomatoes (without the juice) and crush them with a wooden spoon. Reserve the juice for thinning the sauce later if desired. Cover and simmer gently for an hour.
instructions.3: Before serving, break the eggs on top of the gently simmering sauce. Cover the skillet and poach the eggs for 3-5 minutes until they are cooked to your desired doneness.
instructions.4: Garnish with chopped parsley. Serve the dish in the pot it was cooked in.

w-ma-023.culturalNotes: Shakshouka is a popular dish in Morocco and North African countries, typically served as a breakfast or light lunch.
